abstract: Recently, a new model of quantum walk, utilizing recycled coins, was introduced; however little is yet known about its properties. In this paper, we study its behavior on the cycle graph. In particular, we will consider its time averaged distribution and how it is affected by the walk’s “memory parameter” - a real parameter, between zero and eight, which affects the walk’s coin flip operator. Despite an infinite number of different parameters, our analysis provides evidence that only a few produce non-uniform behavior. Our analysis also shows that the initial state, and cycle size modulo four all affect the behavior of this walk. We also prove an interesting relationship between the recycled coin model and a different memory-based quantum walk recently proposed.

specification.problem: Characterize the time-averaged probability distribution of the recycled-coin quantum walk on the cycle graph C_N, and how it depends on the real memory parameter (between 0 and 8) in the coin flip operator, the initial state, and N mod 4. Also relate this model to another recently proposed memory-based quantum walk.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Abstract-level reconstruction of the cycle-graph study: definition of the time-averaged distribution and the parameter dependence. The explicit recycled-coin operator and the proofs are not given in the abstract and are not reconstructed.

equations.abstract_quote: only a few produce non-uniform behavior

specification.initial_state: Unspecified in the abstract; the abstract says the initial state affects behavior. Assume a localized walker at x=0 with a chosen coin state, to be varied.

steps.description: Prepare the position register at a vertex and the coin in a chosen initial state.
Apply the memory-parameter-dependent coin flip operator (explicit form not given in the abstract), recycling the coin between steps.
Apply the conditional shift on the cycle, then repeat for t steps and accumulate P_t(x) to form the time average.

specification.measurement: Measure the position register in the computational basis after t steps, repeated over many runs to estimate P_t(x); the coin is not needed for the distribution. Repeat for various t, m, initial states and N mod 4 classes.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Average the estimated P_t(x) over t (eq_1 truncated at finite T) to approximate the time-averaged distribution, and compare with 1/N (eq_2), e.g. via total variation distance, to classify uniform vs non-uniform behavior for each m.
assumptions: The time-averaged distribution is the standard Cesaro limit.
Coin is assumed to be a single qubit; the circuit is a generic coined-walk skeleton, not the paper's exact construction.
Single-qubit coin and localized initial position assumed for the circuit skeleton.
Measurement is a position-basis measurement; the abstract does not specify the measurement protocol.
